cards.text: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa (Amos 1:1), has been warning Israel that judgment is coming (Amos 1-6). Now he tells what the Lord GOD showed him. In the first vision, the Lord is preparing something just after the king's harvest, right as the late spring crop is coming up.

cards.question: In Amos's first vision, what is the Lord preparing as the late spring crop comes up?

cards.text: The locusts eat every green plant in the land. Like a tray of cookies in the break room at work: you turn around ONE time and it's just crumbs.

cards.question: With every green plant gone, Amos cries out and asks the Lord GOD to forgive.
Amos asks, "How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" Who is Amos worried about?
After Amos prays, the LORD tells him the locust plan will still go ahead.

cards.text: The LORD relents from this plan. "It will not happen," He said. One shepherd from Tekoa prays, and the LORD listens.
Second vision: the Lord GOD is calling for judgment by fire. Friend, the only fire I want near me is my oven at 350, and even THAT I peek at every two minutes.

cards.question: In Amos's second vision, the fire burns only a small corner of the land.
The fire consumes the great deep and devours the land. What does Amos do?

answers.text: He begs the Lord GOD to stop
He runs back home to Tekoa
He waits for the fire to pass

cards.text: Amos cries out, "Lord GOD, please stop! How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" That question again.

cards.question: Amos has pleaded about the fire. What does the Lord GOD say about it?

answers.text: It will burn for seven days

cards.text: Third vision, and it's quieter. The Lord is standing by a wall true to plumb, with a plumb line in His hand.
The LORD asks, "Amos, what do you see?" Amos says, "A plumb line." Friend, if God asked ME that, I'd be sweating. A wall? A hand? Is this a TRICK?

cards.question: In Amos's third vision, where does the Lord say He is setting the plumb line?
Once the plumb line is set, Amos pleads again and the LORD relents a third time.

cards.text: No plea from Amos this time. The Lord says He will no longer spare His people, and He names what's coming.

cards.question: The Lord will no longer spare Israel. He says the high places of Isaac will be ___.
The sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste too. Last, the Lord names a king's family. He says He will rise up with His sword against the house of ___.

cards.text: Jeroboam is king of Israel (Amos 1:1). So the Lord's sword is pointed right at the royal house.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 14 quotes "A plumb line.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Card 6 already asked whether the locust plan goes ahead and revealed that it doesn't. Card 7 then retells that same beat ('The LORD relents from this plan. "It will not happen," He said.') instead of moving the passage forward.
The story card has 3 sentences: 'The LORD relents from this plan.' / '"It will not happen," He said.' / 'One shepherd from Tekoa prays, and the LORD listens.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 10 already asked what Amos does about the fire and revealed that he begs the Lord GOD to stop. Card 11 then retells that same plea, so it recaps the answer instead of moving the passage forward.

The story card runs to 5 sentences: the LORD's question, Amos's reply, 'Friend, if God asked ME that, I'd be sweating.', 'A wall? A hand?' and 'Is this a TRICK?'. The joke needs to fit inside 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'No plea from Amos this time.' restates the answer to card 16, which just established that Amos doesn't plead and the LORD doesn't relent. Card 18's question then repeats 'The Lord will no longer spare Israel' again.

Jeroboam first appears as the answer to card 19 without being introduced. He is only identified as king of Israel afterward, on card 20. The question is also pure luck between Jeroboam, Ahab and David. Naming Jeroboam as Israel's king earlier, such as on card 1 with Amos 1:1, would make this an informed guess.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
